# Block reference

<!-- Generated by tools/node_docs.py from `macromagi nodes`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every block MacroMagi offers, with its ports and settings. **Flow** ports order execution (top and bottom of a block); **value** ports carry results (left and right).

The `id` under each heading is the block's type as written in `.magi` files.

## Flow

Where a macro starts, waits, loops, branches and stops, and the pieces it is built from.

### Function

`flow.call`

Runs the blocks under a Definition block, then carries on from here.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: yes
- Value inputs: **Input** (any value)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Definition | definition | none |  |

### Decision

`flow.decision`

Chooses which branch to follow. Each case has a condition input on the left; the first case whose condition is true wins. If none is true, “Else” is followed.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: **one per case**, **Else**
- Value inputs: **one condition per case** (true/false)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cases | list of cases | one case |  |

### Definition

`flow.define`

The start of a reusable piece of a macro. Build it once under this block, then run it from anywhere with a Function block. Never started by Run or a hotkey.

- Flow out: yes

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Name | text | My function |  |
| Input goes into variable | variable | none | What is wired into a Function block's Input is stored in this variable before the definition runs. |

### Wait

`flow.delay`

Pauses for a set time before continuing.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: yes

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Duration | duration | 500 ms |  |
| Random ± | duration | 0 ms | Vary each wait by a random amount up to this, so the timing looks less mechanical. |

### Log

`flow.log`

Writes a line to the console. Handy for checking which path a macro took.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: yes
- Value inputs: **Value** (any value)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Message | text | empty |  |

### Rate

`flow.rate`

Does a list of inputs one after another, a set time apart – a whole chain of Input and Wait blocks in one. The time can come from a variable or be wired in.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: yes
- Value inputs: **Rate (ms)** (number)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Time between steps | duration | 100 ms |  |
| Hold taps for | duration | 30 ms |  |
| Steps | list of inputs | one left click |  |

### Repeat

`flow.repeat`

Runs the blocks under “Loop” over and over, then continues from “Done”. When the looped branch reaches its end it automatically returns here.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: **Loop**, **Done**
- Value inputs: **Condition** (true/false)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Repeat | choice | A number of times | Options: A number of times; Until stopped; Until the condition is true; While the condition is true. |
| Times | whole number | 10 × |  |

### Start

`flow.start`

Where a macro begins. A macro can have several Start blocks; each one runs independently and can have its own hotkey.

- Flow out: yes

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hotkey | hotkey | none | Any keyboard key, mouse button or gamepad button, alone or combined. |
| Hotkey behaviour | choice | Toggle | Options: Toggle – press to start, press again to stop; Hold – run while the hotkey is held; Press – start on every press. |
| Start with the Run button | on/off | on | Turn off for blocks that should only ever be started by their hotkey. |

### Stop

`flow.stop`

Ends the macro here – or only this branch, or the loop it is in, or jumps to another block.

- Flow in: yes

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stop | choice | This Start block | Options: This Start block; The whole macro; This branch – go on with the loop's next round; The loop – continue from its Done; Here, and continue from another block. |
| Continue from | block | none | The block to run next. |

### Wait Until

`flow.wait_until`

Pauses until its condition becomes true, checking at a regular interval.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: **Then**, **Timed out**
- Value inputs: **Condition** (true/false)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Check every | duration | 100 ms |  |
| Give up after | duration | 0 ms | Zero means wait for as long as it takes. |

## Input

Sending keyboard and mouse input.

### Input

`input.action`

Sends input: a key, a mouse click, a move, a scroll or typed text. Add several inputs to one block to perform them at the same time, like Ctrl + C.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: yes
- Value inputs: **Position** (screen position)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Inputs | list of inputs | one left click |  |
| Hold time | duration | 30 ms | How long taps and clicks stay pressed before they are released. |

### Auto Click

`input.autoclick`

Clicks (or presses keys) over and over at a steady speed, with everything the Auto Clicker tab offers: speed variation, duty cycle, limits, corner and edge stops.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: yes

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clicking | Auto Clicker settings | left click, 10 per second, until stopped |  |

### Auto Typer

`input.autotype`

Types text, character by character, at a speed that can vary like a person's. The text is its own setting, a variable it is linked to, or whatever is wired into “Text”.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: yes
- Value inputs: **Text** (text)
- Value outputs: **Characters typed** (number)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Text | text | empty | What to type. A value wired into “Text” is typed instead. |
| Characters per second | number | 12 per second | A person types about 5 per second (60 words a minute). |
| Speed variation | percentage | 30% | How much each pause between characters may differ, so the rhythm is not mechanical. |
| Pause after punctuation | on/off | on | A longer pause after . , ! ? ; and :, as people make. |
| Typos | percentage | 0% | The chance of mistyping a letter and correcting it with Backspace. 0% types it right. |
| Trim spaces at the ends | on/off | off |  |
| Skip the first | whole number | 0 characters |  |
| Type at most | whole number | 0 characters | 0 types everything. |
| Line breaks | choice | Press Enter | Options: Press Enter; Press Shift+Enter – a new line in a chat box; Type a space; Leave them out. |
| Press Enter at the end | on/off | off |  |

### Play Recording

`input.recording`

Replays recorded input with its original timing: every key and button is pressed and released exactly when it was during recording.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: yes

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Recording | recording | none |  |
| Speed | number | 1 × |  |
| Replay mouse movement | on/off | on |  |
| Mouse movement as | choice | As recorded (smart) | Games with a first-person camera lock the pointer and read how far the mouse moves. If the camera turns once and then stops, choose relative motion. Options: As recorded (smart); Screen positions; Relative motion – for games. |

## Vision

Looking at the screen. These are value blocks: they have no place in the order of execution and are evaluated whenever another block reads them.

### Color Detection

`vision.find_color`

Looks for a color on screen. “Found” is true when at least one pixel in the search area matches; “Position” is the first matching pixel.

- Value outputs: **Found** (true/false), **Position** (screen position)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Color | color | #FF3B30 |  |
| Tolerance | whole number | 16 | How far red, green and blue may each be off and still count as a match. |
| Search area | screen area | whole screen |  |
| Display | display | 1 (primary) | The display searched when there is no search area. |

### Image Detection

`vision.find_image`

Looks for an image on screen. “Found” is true when a match at least as similar as the accuracy setting exists; “Position” is the centre of the best match. Wire “Found” into a Decision or Wait Until, and “Position” into an Input to click it.

- Value outputs: **Found** (true/false), **Position** (screen position), **Similarity** (number), **Which image** (text), **Its group** (text), **How many** (number)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Images | list of images | none yet | Several images can be looked for at once, in order of priority: the first one found is the one reported. Put images in a group to give them a search area of their own. |
| Found when | choice | Any image is there | Options: Any image is there; Every image is there. |
| Search area | screen area | whole screen | For every image without an area of its own or of its group. A smaller area is faster and avoids false matches elsewhere on screen. |
| Display | display | 1 (primary) | The display searched when there is no search area. |
| Accuracy | percentage | 80% | How closely the screen must match the image. 100% demands a pixel-perfect match. |
| Detail | choice | Full | Shrinks the screen and the images before comparing them. Less detail is much faster but can miss small or fine images. Options: Full – most accurate; Half – about 4× faster; A third – about 9× faster; A quarter – fastest. |

### Text Scan

`vision.read_text`

Reads the text in an area of the screen (optical character recognition). “Text” is what it reads, line by line. With text to look for, “Found” says whether it is there and “Position” is where; “Number” is the first number in the text. Uses the text recognition built into Windows.

- Value outputs: **Found** (true/false), **Text** (text), **Position** (screen position), **Number** (number)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Area | screen area | whole screen | The area to read. A small area around the text is faster and reads more reliably. |
| Display | display | 1 (primary) | The display read when there is no area. |
| Look for | text | empty | Text that makes “Found” true. Empty: any text does. |
| Match upper and lower case | on/off | off |  |
| Enlarge | choice | No | Text recognition needs letters at least about 10 pixels tall. Options: No – the text is a normal size; Twice – small text; Three times – tiny text. |
| Language | text | empty | A language tag such as en-US or de-DE. Empty: the languages of your Windows. |

## Sound

Listening to what the computer plays, or to the microphone. Value blocks, like the vision blocks.

### Sound Detection

`sound.level`

Listens for sound that is loud enough – and, optionally, within a pitch range. “Detected” is true while it is heard; “Loudness” is in dB (0 is the loudest possible, quiet sound is around -60) and “Pitch” in Hz. Wire “Detected” into a Wait Until or a Decision.

- Value outputs: **Detected** (true/false), **Loudness (dB)** (number), **Pitch (Hz)** (number)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Listen to | choice | What the computer plays | Options: What the computer plays; Microphone. |
| Microphone | microphone | the default | Which microphone to listen to; the system's default when none is chosen. |
| Loud enough at | number | -30 dB | 0 dB is the loudest sound possible. Normal sound is around -30 dB, quiet sound -60 dB. |
| Only within a pitch range | on/off | off |  |
| Lowest pitch | number | 200 Hz |  |
| Highest pitch | number | 2000 Hz | The strongest frequency heard must be in this range. A man's voice is around 100–150 Hz, a whistle 1000–3000 Hz. |
| Measure the last | duration | 200 ms | Longer smooths out short clicks and gaps; shorter reacts faster. |

### Sound Recognition

`sound.match`

Listens for particular sounds – a notification, an alarm, a voice line – that you upload as sound files. “Found” is true once one is heard at least as closely as the accuracy setting, however loud it is played; “Which sound” says which one was recognised last. Each time a sound is heard counts once.

- Value outputs: **Found** (true/false), **Similarity** (number), **Which sound** (text), **Its group** (text), **How many** (number)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Listen to | choice | What the computer plays | Options: What the computer plays; Microphone. |
| Microphone | microphone | the default | Which microphone to listen to; the system's default when none is chosen. |
| Sounds | list of sounds | none yet | WAV, MP3, OGG or FLAC files; the first 10 seconds of each are used. Short and distinctive works best. Put sounds in a group to give them an accuracy of their own. |
| Found when | choice | Any sound is heard | Options: Any sound is heard; Every sound has been heard. |
| Accuracy | percentage | 75% | How closely what is heard must match. Lower it if the sound is missed, raise it if other sounds set it off. |
| Recognise from the first | duration | 0 ms | 0 waits for the whole sound. A second or two is enough for most sounds, and long sounds are then recognised while they are still playing. |

## AI

Small vision models prepared in the Magic tab, run on what is on screen.

### AI Model

`ai.classify`

Shows part of the screen to an AI model once and gives its answer: the likeliest class, how sure the model is, and whether the model's setup says to act on it.

- Value outputs: **Act** (true/false), **Answer** (text), **Class number** (number), **Confidence** (number), **Delay (ms)** (number)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Model | AI model | none | A model prepared in the Magic tab. Use “Use in Macro” there, or load a .magic file. |
| Model settings | model settings | the model's own | The model's own adjustable settings, changed for this block only. |
| Display | display | 1 (primary) | For models that look at the middle of the screen: which display. |

### AI Watch

`ai.watch`

Keeps showing part of the screen to an AI model and does what the model is set up to do – for example press a key the moment it sees the right thing. Each time it acts, the blocks under “Acted” run (with “Times acted” and “Last answer” up to date), then it watches again. Runs until the macro stops, or for as long as set; then it continues from “Done”.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: **Acted**, **Done**
- Value outputs: **Times acted** (number), **Last answer** (text)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Model | AI model | none | A model prepared in the Magic tab. Use “Use in Macro” there, or load a .magic file. |
| Model settings | model settings | the model's own | The model's own adjustable settings, changed for this block only. |
| Display | display | 1 (primary) | For models that look at the middle of the screen: which display. |
| Press the model's key | on/off | on | Off: the model only watches and runs the blocks under “Acted” – try it safely, or do something else than pressing the key. |
| Stop after | duration | 0 ms | 0 keeps watching until the macro is stopped. |
| Looks per second | number | 0 | 0 looks as often as the computer can. A limit saves power. |

## Window

Working with program windows.

### Switch to Window

`window.focus`

Brings a program's window to the front (restoring it if it is minimised) and waits until it is ready for input. Knows how windowed, borderless and exclusive fullscreen programs behave, or works it out itself.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: **Switched**, **Not found**
- Value outputs: **Screen type** (text)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Window | text | empty | Part of the window's title, or of the program's name, e.g. “Minecraft” or “game.exe”. |
| Find it by | choice | Window title | Options: Window title; Program name. |
| Screen type | choice | Detect automatically | Exclusive fullscreen programs need longer to come back after a switch. Options: Detect automatically; Windowed; Borderless fullscreen; Exclusive fullscreen. |
| Keep looking for | duration | 2000 ms |  |

## Variables

Named values a macro reads and changes while it runs. Any setting of any block can also follow a variable (the link button next to it).

### Counter

`var.counter`

Counts passes: adds the step to a variable each time it runs. When a limit is set and reached, “Reached” is followed and counting starts again from zero.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: **Next**, **Reached**
- Value outputs: **Count** (number)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Variable | variable | none |  |
| Step | number | 1 |  |
| Limit | number | 0 | Zero: count for ever, never take “Reached”. |

### Variable

`var.get`

The current value of a variable, for any block that reads values.

- Value outputs: **Value** (any value)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Variable | variable | none |  |

### Set Variable

`var.set`

Changes a variable: sets it, adds to it, multiplies it… Every block bound to the variable follows the new value.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: yes
- Value inputs: **Value** (any value)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Variable | variable | none |  |
| Do | choice | Set to | Options: Set to; Add; Subtract; Multiply by; Divide by; Add text to the end. |
| Value | text | empty | Used when nothing is wired into the Value input. 42, true or any text. |

## Logic

Combining and producing values: true/false, numbers and text.

### Random Chance

`logic.chance`

True some of the time, at random. Use it to make a macro less predictable.

- Value outputs: **Result** (true/false)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chance of true | percentage | 50% |  |

### Compare

`logic.compare`

True when A relates to B in the chosen way: equal, less, greater, contains… Numbers compare as numbers, everything else as text.

- Value inputs: **A** (any value), **B** (any value)
- Value outputs: **Result** (true/false)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Operation | choice | A equals B | Options: A equals B; A is not B; A is less than B; A is at most B; A is greater than B; A is at least B; A contains B; A starts with B; A ends with B. |
| B | text | empty | Used when nothing is wired into B. |

### Logic

`logic.gate`

Combines true/false values: AND, OR, XOR, or NOT (which only uses input A).

- Value inputs: **A** (true/false), **B** (true/false)
- Value outputs: **Result** (true/false)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Operation | choice | A and B | Options: A and B; A or B; Exactly one of A, B; Not A. |

### Math

`logic.math`

Calculates with numbers: add, subtract, multiply, divide, round, random… A and B come from their inputs, or from the numbers typed here when nothing is wired.

- Value inputs: **A** (number), **B** (number)
- Value outputs: **Result** (number)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Operation | choice | A + B | Options: A + B; A − B; A × B; A ÷ B; Remainder of A ÷ B; A to the power of B; The smaller of A, B; The larger of A, B; A rounded; A rounded down; A rounded up; A without its sign; Random number from A to B. |
| A | number | 0 |  |
| B | number | 0 |  |

### Text

`logic.text`

Works with text: joins it, measures it, changes case, replaces words, or reads a number from it.

- Value inputs: **A** (any value), **B** (any value)
- Value outputs: **Result** (any value)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Operation | choice | A followed by B | Options: A followed by B; Length of A; A in capitals; A in small letters; A without spaces around it; A with B replaced; A as a number. |
| A | text | empty | Used when nothing is wired into A. |
| B | text | empty | Used when nothing is wired into B. |
| Replace with | text | empty |  |

## System

The clipboard and notifications.

### Clipboard

`system.clipboard`

The text on the clipboard. Wire it into Set Variable to keep it, or into any block that reads text.

- Value outputs: **Text** (text)

### Notification

`system.notify`

Plays a short sound and shows a desktop notification – for example when a long macro has finished.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: yes
- Value inputs: **Value** (any value)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Title | text | MacroMagi |  |
| Message | text | Done | Whatever is wired into Value is added to the end. |
| Play a sound | on/off | on |  |
| Show a desktop notification | on/off | on |  |

## Script

Your own code as a step of the macro.

### Python Script

`script.python` · Python engine only

Runs your own Python code as a step of the macro. The script can send input, read the screen and compute a result for other blocks. Needs the Python engine.

- Flow in: yes
- Flow out: yes
- Value inputs: **Value** (any value)
- Value outputs: **Result** (any value)

| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Code | code | a commented starter script |  |
| Store the result in | variable | none | When the script ends, `result` is stored in this variable. |

## Notes

Explanations on the canvas. They never run.

### Comment

`note.comment`

A note on the canvas. It does nothing when the macro runs. Resize it by its corner, fold it by its arrow.



| Setting | Kind | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Text | text | A note about this part of the macro. |  |
| Width | number | 240 |  |
| Height | number | 120 |  |
| Folded | on/off | off |  |
| Color | color |  | Pick a color or type #RRGGBB. Empty (the reset button) uses the theme color. |
